findings.text: Nothing tests the publication gate the node added: the three focused tests exercise autotune_file_count and grep the launcher for one literal line, so deleting the count-autotune invocation or inverting the `if [[ "${status}" -eq 0 ]]` condition would publish a pin carrying autotune files while every test stays green. The head arm would have to run the payload and assert that no prewarm-latest.json is written.

autotune_file_count re-implements, more narrowly, the autotune-entry count that benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:104 inventory already owns via is_autotune_path:108; the lane could read inventory(served_directory)["autotune_entries"] instead of forking the rule, so the two counters can drift on what counts as an autotune file.

test_identity_row_allows_numerical_failure_after_cache_write asserts a literal substring of prewarm.sh, so it reddens on a pure reformat and says nothing about the behaviour it names; it also does not distinguish the identity row from the lane row, both of which carry the flag.

The republished pin names source_revision ba0609243f176b4ec2e395f696d437f435362e74 (pin document and lane-resolver-retry-20261105.log:2) while main moved to ccaacf500e8e4150d6721d80adea433acb1904e9 during the 52-minute job, so a lane run at current main prints PINNED_REVISION_MISMATCH and no cache-hit rate has been measured against the new pin; this belongs to the §4 pin-measuring node.
